literal_meaning: The analogy of ants being mad for jaggery.
explanation: The ants’ pull towards sweetness supplies a picture of someone’s marked eagerness or greed. The dictionary allows both interest and greed, so the comparison need not carry the same accusation on every occasion. A playful comment about enthusiasm can turn sharp when the attraction is self-serving. The object of desire need not be food.
meaning_odia: ଗୁଡ଼ ପ୍ରତି ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆକର୍ଷଣକୁ ଧରି ଜଣକର ବିଶେଷ ଆଗ୍ରହ କିମ୍ବା ଲୋଭ ବୁଝାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଦୁଇଟି ଅର୍ଥର ସୁଯୋଗ ରଖିଛି। ତେଣୁ ପ୍ରତିଥର ଏହାକୁ କଠୋର ଲୋଭର ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିଦେଲେ କଥାର ସ୍ୱର ବଦଳିଯିବ। ଅବସର ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ନେଇ ହାଲୁକା ଥଟ୍ଟା ହୋଇପାରେ, କିମ୍ବା ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ବ୍ୟାକୁଳତାକୁ ବିନ୍ଧିପାରେ।
english_summary: An attraction can be playful eagerness or pointedly described greed.
odia_summary: ବିଶେଷ ଆଗ୍ରହ ବା ଲୋଭକୁ ଗୁଡ଼ ପ୍ରତି ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆକର୍ଷଣ ସହ ତୁଳନା।

title: Drawn to jaggery like ants
usage_example: A friend who never misses a book sale is already at the door before it opens. A companion laughs and uses the ants-and-jaggery analogy. (Original imagined use, choosing the source’s interest rather than greed sense.)
cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly supplies interest or greed as applications. The new example chooses interest; no origin story, popularity measurement or universal claim about ant behaviour is added.
